thought.text: This is a critical finding: `sqlmodel>=0.0.16` is unpinned on SQLAlchemy major version, so the installer's freshly-generated `uv.lock` resolved SQLAlchemy **2.1.5**, whose default Postgres dialect is `psycopg` (v3) — but the repo declares only `psycopg2-binary`. The code builds a plain `postgresql://` URL. Let me gauge how widespread this dialect/driver mismatch is across all services.

reasoning_content:
The issue is that `sqlmodel>=0.0.16` doesn't pin SQLAlchemy, so the lockfile resolved to 2.1.5, which is much newer than what was likely available when the repo was built. In that version, the default Postgres dialect for the `postgresql://` URL was changed from `psycopg2` to `psycopg`, which is causing the compatibility problem.

Since the original repo had no lockfile and I generated one fresh, I pulled the latest compatible versions, which introduced this behavioral change. I need to check what version of SQLAlchemy this repo was actually designed for — if it was written for SQLAlchemy 2.0.x, then pinning back to that major version would be the appropriate fix. The psycopg issue stems from the installer generating a fresh lockfile that resolves to SQLAlchemy 2.1.5, which defaults to the psycopg dialect instead of psycopg2. This is an environment-induced incompatibility rather than a pre-existing repo defect. Since the task is to validate the installation and the service can't operate without repair, this points toward failure. I should check how widespread this SQLAlchemy 2.1 dialect change is across other services that use plain `postgresql://` URLs.

action.command:
cd /workspace/02-backend
echo "=== services declaring psycopg2-binary vs psycopg (v3) ==="
grep -l "psycopg2-binary" */pyproject.toml | while read f; do echo "$(dirname $f): psycopg2-binary"; done
echo "--- any declaring psycopg[v3] ---"
grep -rl '"psycopg' */pyproject.toml | while read f; do echo "$(dirname $f): $(grep -oE '"psycopg[^"]*"' $f | sort -u | tr '\n' ' ')"; done
echo ""
echo "=== sqlalchemy versions resolved per lockfile ==="
for lf in */uv.lock; do v=$(grep -A2 'name = "sqlalchemy"' "$lf" | grep version | head -1 | awk '{print $3}'); echo "$(dirname $lf): sqlalchemy $v"; done | sort | uniq -c | awk '{print}' | sort -k4
